Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 20, verse 1:

Naming of the Surah

• It is called Ta-Ha, because it opens with these two letters. This combination of disjointed letters (al-huruf al-muqatta'a) does not occur anywhere else in the Noble Qur'an except in this place.

Some Objectives of the Surah

• Concern for the Messenger (ﷺ) by strengthening his resolve and fortifying his spirit, so that he remains steadfast in his call despite the plots and obstinacy he encounters, and guidance for him regarding his duty and the limits of his responsibility: his mission is only to convey and remind, to warn and to give glad tidings.

• Praise of the Noble Qur'an, that it is a revelation from Allah to guide those who are receptive to guidance, and affirmation of the Prophet's (ﷺ) message, that it resembles the message of the greatest messenger before him, whose mention is widespread among the people, and the presenting of an example of the descent of the Qur'an upon Muhammad (ﷺ) with the speech of Allah to Musa (Moses).

• Discussion of the upbringing of Musa, Allah's support for him, his victory over Pharaoh through proof and miracles, the turning away of Pharaoh's plot from Musa and his followers, and the explanation of the punishment that befell Pharaoh and his people.

• Reminding people of the enmity of Satan toward humankind through what the story of the creation of Adam contains, the explanation of the evil recompense in the Hereafter for those who follow Satan, and warning them of the evil punishment in this world.

• Affirmation of resurrection and recompense, and mention of some of the terrors of the Day of Resurrection.

[The Tafsir]

﴿Ta-Ha﴾ The discussion of the disjointed letters has already preceded at the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah.
We did not send down the Qur'an to you, O Messenger, to make you suffer hardship through what you have no capacity to bear of action.

But We sent it down as an admonition, so that whoever fears the punishment of Allah may be reminded by it, and thereby guard himself against that punishment by performing the obligatory duties and avoiding the forbidden things.

**Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar, "The Easy Tafsir") on surah 20, verse 4:**

﴿This Qur'an is a revelation from Allah, who created the earth and the lofty heavens.﴾
﴿The Most Merciful is established upon the Throne﴾. Meaning: He rose above and was exalted, in a manner of istiwa' (establishment, lofty elevation) befitting His majesty and greatness.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 20, verse 6:

To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens, whatever is on the earth, whatever is between them, and whatever is beneath the soil: He is their Creator, their Owner, and their Disposer.

If you speak aloud, O Messenger, or keep it hidden, then indeed Allah is not concealed from Him by anything: He knows the secret and what is even more hidden than the secret, such as what you speak to yourself within your soul.
Allah, there is no deity worthy of worship except Him. To Him alone belong the most beautiful names.
Has the story of Musa, son of Imran (peace be upon him), reached you, O Messenger, as he was coming from Madyan to Egypt?

When he saw a fire at night, he said to his family: "Wait, for I have seen a fire; perhaps I can bring you from it a burning brand, so that you may warm yourselves by it, or find at the fire someone who can guide us to the way."

When Musa reached that fire, Allah called out to him: "O Musa, indeed I am your Lord, so take off your sandals. Indeed you are now in the valley of Tuwa, which I have blessed." This was in preparation for his conversing with his Lord.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 20, verse 14:

"Indeed, I am Allah. There is no deity worthy of worship except Me, without any partner. So worship Me alone, and establish the prayer to remember Me in it."

The Hour in which people will be resurrected is coming and must certainly occur. I almost conceal it from Myself; so how could any of the creatures know it? (This is so) that every soul may be recompensed for what it did in the world, whether good or evil.

So let not one who does not believe in it (the Hour) and who does not prepare for it turn you away from it, O Moses, and so you would perish, for he follows his own desire and denies it.

Wait, that rendering is not faithful to the sentence as it stands. Here is the translation:

Let not the one who does not believe in it (the Hour) and does not work for it turn you away from belief in it and from preparing for it, O Moses. He follows his own desire, so he denies it, and you would perish.

Moses said to him: "Our Lord is the One who gave everything its creation, fitting for it and indicating the excellence of His craftsmanship, and then guided every creature to the complete guidance of benefiting from what God created for it."

Pharaoh said to Moses, by way of sophistry and contentiousness: "Then what is the matter with the earlier nations? And what of the generations of the past, for they preceded us in denial and disbelief?"

Moses said to Pharaoh: What you have asked about is not what we are concerned with. Rather, the knowledge of those past generations and what they did is with my Lord, recorded in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz), and I have no knowledge of it. My Lord neither errs (la yadillu) in His actions and His judgments, nor forgets anything of what He has known of them.

He is the One who made the earth a smooth, accessible place for you to benefit from, and made for you within it many roads, and sent down rain from the sky, and by it brought forth various kinds of plants.

Eat, O people, of the good things We have caused to grow for you, and let your livestock and cattle graze. Indeed, in all that has been mentioned are signs of God's power and a call to His oneness and to worshipping Him alone, for those of sound minds.
From the earth We created you, O people, and into it We will return you after death, and from it We will bring you out alive once more for reckoning and recompense.
And We certainly showed Pharaoh all of Our signs and proofs, those that indicate Our divinity, Our power, and the truthfulness of Moses' message, but he denied them and refused to accept the truth.
Pharaoh said: "Have you come to us, O Moses, to drive us out of our land with this magic of yours?"
So We will surely bring you magic like your magic. So set between us and you an appointed meeting that neither we nor you will fail to keep, at a place equally level between us and you.
Moses said to Pharaoh: "Your appointment for the gathering is the day of the festival, when the people adorn themselves and assemble from every direction and region at the time of mid-morning."
Pharaoh turned away and withdrew, rejecting what Moses had brought him of the truth. He gathered his sorcerers, then came to the appointed meeting.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 20, verse 90:

Harun (Aaron) had already said to the Children of Israel, before Musa (Moses) returned to them: "O my people, you are only being tested through this calf; so that the believer among you may be distinguished from the disbeliever. Indeed, your Lord is the Most Merciful (al-Rahman), not other than Him. So follow me in what I call you to of worshipping Allah, and obey my command in following His law."
The worshippers of the calf among them said: "We will not cease to remain devoted to the worship of the calf until Moses returns to us."

Moses said to his brother Aaron: "What prevented you, when you saw them going astray from their religion, from following me, so that you would come after me and leave them behind? Did you disobey my command, in what I charged you with, of taking my place (in leading them) and setting things right after me?"

Moses said to his brother Aaron: "What prevented you, when you saw them going astray from their religion, from following me, so that you would come after me and leave them behind? Did you disobey my command, in what I charged you with, of taking my place (in leading them) and setting things right after me?"

Then Moses seized his brother Aaron by the beard and head, dragging him toward himself. Aaron said to him: "O son of my mother, do not seize my beard or the hair of my head. I feared that, if I had stayed behind with them and you had come back to me, you would say: 'You caused division among the Children of Israel, and did not keep my charge by caring well for them.'"
Musa said to the Samiri: "What is your business, O Samiri? And what led you to do what you did?"

Al-Samiri said: "I saw what they did not see, namely Jibril (peace be upon him), riding a horse at the time they came out of the sea and Pharaoh and his soldiers drowned. So I took a handful of dust from the hoofprint of Jibril's horse and threw it onto the jewelry from which I made the calf. Then it became a calf, a body with a lowing sound, as a trial and a test. And thus my ego that commands to evil adorned this deed for me."

Musa said to the Samiri: "Go, for your punishment in this worldly life is that you will live shunned; you will say to everyone, 'Do not touch me, and do not let anyone touch me.' And for you there is an appointed term in the Hereafter for your torment and punishment; Allah will not fail to fulfil it for you, and you will certainly meet it. Now look at your god to which you devoted yourself in worship: we will surely burn it with fire, then we will scatter it into the sea, scattering it so that the wind carries it away, until no trace of it remains."
"Indeed, your God, O people, is only Allah, besides whom there is no deity worthy of worship, and His knowledge encompasses all things."

As We have related to you, O Messenger, the accounts of Musa (Moses), Fir'awn (Pharaoh) and their people, so We inform you of the accounts of those who came before you. And We have given you this Qur'an from Our presence as a reminder for whoever will be mindful.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 20, verse 100:

Whoever turns away from this Qur'an, does not believe in it, and does not act upon what is in it, then he will come to his Lord on the Day of Resurrection carrying a great burden of sin.
Remaining eternally in the punishment, and that burden of sins is evil for them, as it has brought them to the Fire.

On the Day the angel blows into the Horn (al-Qarn) for the Blast of Resurrection, We will gather the disbelievers on that Day with their eyes blue-grey, their complexions and their eyes changed by the severity of the events and terrors.
They whisper among themselves, some of them saying to others: "You remained in this worldly life only ten days."

We know best what they say and what they whisper, when the most knowledgeable and most rational of them says: "You did not remain [in the world] except for a single day," because of how short the life of this world seems to them on the Day of Resurrection.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 20, verse 105:

And your people ask you, O Messenger, about the fate of the mountains on the Day of Resurrection. Say to them: My Lord will uproot them from their places and make them like scattered dust.
Then He will leave the earth at that time flat, level and smooth, with no vegetation in it. The one who looks at it will see no slope, no rise, and no depression in its evenness.
Then He will leave the earth at that time flat, level and smooth, with no vegetation in it. The one who looks at it will see no slope, no rise, and no depression in its evenness.

On that Day the people will follow the voice of the caller to the place of standing for Resurrection. There is no escape from the summons of the caller, for it is true and sincere for all creation. The voices will fall silent in submission to the Most Merciful, so you will hear nothing but a faint whisper.

On that Day, intercession will benefit no one among the creatures, except one for whom the Most Merciful has given permission to intercede, and with whom He is pleased regarding the one for whom intercession is made; and that will only be for the sincere believer.

Allah knows what lies before people of the matter of the Resurrection, and what lies behind them of the matter of this world. His creation cannot encompass Him in knowledge, glory be to Him and exalted.

And the faces of all creatures will be humbled and abased before their Creator, the One who possesses all the attributes of perfect life, as befits His majesty, the One who does not die, who sustains the management of everything, and who is free of need of anything other than Himself. And whoever associated with God anyone from His creation has certainly lost on the Day of Resurrection.

And whoever does righteous deeds while being a believer in his Lord, then he will not fear any injustice, through an increase in his bad deeds, nor any diminishing, through a decrease in his good deeds.

And thus We have made the believers desire righteous deeds and warned the disbelievers against persisting in their sins and their disbelief in Our signs. We have sent down this Qur'an in the Arabic tongue so that they may understand it, and We have set forth in it various kinds of warning, in hope that they may fear their Lord, or that this Qur'an may produce in them a reminder, so that they may take heed and be admonished.

Then exalted is Allah, glorified and high above every imperfection, the King whose sovereignty overpowers every king and tyrant, the One who disposes of everything, who is the Truth; His promise is true, His warning is true, and everything from Him is true. "And do not hasten with the Qur'an before its revelation is completed to you" (O Messenger), and do not rush to get ahead of Jibril (Gabriel) in receiving the Qur'an before he has finished it, and say: "My Lord, increase me in knowledge."

We had indeed enjoined upon Adam, before he ate from the tree, that he should not eat from it. And We said to him: "Indeed, Iblis is an enemy to you and to your wife, so let him not drive you both out of the Garden, lest you suffer in this world." Then Satan whispered to him, and Adam obeyed him and forgot the commandment. And We did not find in him steadfast resolve by which he would preserve what he had been commanded.
Remember, O Messenger, when We said to the angels: "Prostrate to Adam," a prostration of greeting and honour. So they obeyed and prostrated, but Iblis refused to prostrate.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 20, verse 117:

We said: "O Adam, indeed this Iblis (Satan) is an enemy to you and to your wife, so beware of him and do not obey him by disobeying Me, lest he expel you both from Paradise, and you will be miserable if you are expelled from it."
Indeed, for you, O Adam, there is a complete blessing and a continuous gift in this Garden: that you will eat and not go hungry, and that you will clothe yourself and not go naked.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 20, verse 119:

And that for you is that you will not thirst in this Paradise, nor will the heat of the sun reach you.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 20, verse 120:

So Satan whispered to Adam, saying: "Shall I direct you to a tree whose fruit, if you eat from it, will make you abide forever, so that you never die, and you will possess a kingdom that never decays and never ends?"

Then Adam and Eve ate from the tree that Allah had forbidden them, so their private parts were exposed to them, though they had been hidden from their eyes. They began to take leaves from the trees of the Garden and stick them over themselves, so as to cover what had been exposed of their private parts. Adam disobeyed the command of his Lord and so went astray by eating from the tree that Allah had forbidden him to approach.
Then Allah chose Adam, brought him near to Himself, accepted his repentance, and guided him to the right path.

God said to Adam and Eve: "Go down from the Garden to the earth, all of you together, along with Iblis. You are enemies to one another. So if guidance and clear proof come to you from Me, then whoever follows My guidance and My clear proof and acts upon them will be rightly guided in this world, and will not be wretched in the Hereafter through the punishment of God."

Whoever turns away from My remembrance, which I send to remind him, will have a constricted and hard life in this world, even if he appears to be among the people of wealth and ease. His grave will be constricted around him and he will be punished in it. On the Day of Resurrection, We will gather him blind, both in sight and in proof.
He who turned away from the remembrance of Allah says: "My Lord, why have You raised me up blind, when I was seeing in the world?"

God said to him (the one who turned away from the remembrance): "I will raise you up blind, because My clear signs came to you, but you turned away from them and did not believe in them. Just as you abandoned them in the world, so today you will be abandoned in the Fire."

Thus do We punish whoever transgresses against himself, disobeys his Lord, and does not believe in His signs, with punishments in this world. But the punishment of the Hereafter, prepared for them, is more painful, more lasting, and more enduring, because it does not end and does not come to an end.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 20, verse 128:

Has it not become clear to your people, O Messenger, the path of guidance, through the multitude of the nations who denied before them whom We destroyed, while they walk through their dwellings and see the traces of their destruction? Indeed, in the multitude of those nations and the traces of their punishment are lessons and admonitions for people of sound intellect.

Had it not been for a word that had already gone forth from your Lord to delay the punishment from them, and for a specified term at which destruction would befall them, it would have immediately cleaved to them in this world, because they deserve it on account of their disbelief.

Therefore be patient, O Messenger, over what those who deny you say of descriptions and falsehoods, and glorify your Lord with His praise before the rising of the sun, meaning the Fajr prayer, and before its setting, meaning the 'Asr prayer, and in the hours of the night, meaning the 'Isha' prayer, and glorify your Lord with His praise at the extremities of the day, meaning the Dhuhr prayer, since its time falls at the end of the first half and the beginning of the second half of the day, and the Maghrib prayer, so that you may be rewarded for these deeds with that with which you will be content.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 20, verse 131:

Do not look longingly at what We have given enjoyment to these polytheists and their like, of various kinds of worldly pleasures. Indeed, they are a fleeting adornment in this worldly life, which We have granted them so that We may test them through it. But the provision of your Lord and His reward are better for you than what We have given them to enjoy, and more lasting, for it never ends and never runs out.

And enjoin your family, O Prophet, to pray, and be patient in performing it. We do not ask you for any provision; We provide for you and grant you sustenance. And the good outcome, in this world and the Hereafter, belongs to the people of taqwa (God-consciousness).

And those who deny you, O Messenger, say: "Why do you not bring us a sign from your Lord that proves your truthfulness?" Has there not come to them this Qur'an, which confirms the truth found in the earlier Scriptures?

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 20, verse 134:

Had We destroyed these deniers with a punishment before sending them a messenger and revealing a Book to them, they would have said: "Our Lord, why did You not send us a messenger from Yourself, so that we might believe him, follow Your signs and Your law, before we were humiliated and disgraced by Your punishment?"

Say, [O Messenger], to these polytheists: "Each of us and you is awaiting the turns of fortune, and to whom victory and success will belong. So wait, and you will know who are the people of the straight path, and who has been guided to the truth, we or you?"
